passages.provision_quote: Sec. 8. (a) Except as provided in subsection (b), a governmental entity may not substantially burden a person's exercise of religion, SEA 101 — Concur 3 even if the burden results from a rule of general applicability. (b) A governmental entity may substantially burden a person's exercise of religion only if the governmental entity demonstrates that application of the burden to the person: (1) is in furtherance of a compelling governmental interest; and (2) is the least restrictive means of furthering that compelling governmental interest.
passages.note: Bill text sets the strict-scrutiny exemption standard that Soliday's vote enacted.
House roll call 305 shows Soliday voting Yea on SB 101's final passage.

rows.reasoning: Soliday voted Yea on SB 101 (2015), a single-subject Religious Freedom Restoration Act whose Sec. 8 bars a governmental entity from substantially burdening a person's exercise of religion unless it meets strict scrutiny, with Sec. 9-10 giving the person a claim or defense for relief from a conflicting law. That is the clause of 'protect religious freedom and allow faith-based exemptions from laws that conflict with sincere religious beliefs,' not the anti-discrimination carve-outs of rungs 1-2 or the complete-organizational-autonomy language of rung 5.
